task: We heard a lot about your native wit, <Ranger>, so we want you to complete a mission that requires this particular quality. Now is the time of the final series of the Intergalactic Tournament in Hyper-jumping Plasma-checker on the <ToPlanet> planet. Our team gained an equal number of points with the humans' team lately (which won the last 3 tournaments), but the turbobus with our players turned over in the Tyrcaucases Mountains and now we have all chances to lose again. The tournament authorities decided to postpone the final game till <Date> and we request you to fly to <ToStar> and tear the humans' team to pieces! The award in the amount of <Money> credits is guaranteed.
success: Congratulations, ranger <Ranger>! You won the final game on Plasma-checkers for our planet, so now they will respect us for being the most intellectual planet in the Galaxy! Here are your <Money> credits, you deserved them!
loc.4.0:
You went to the <ToPlanet>' sports centre right upon arrival to the planet.

 - Hewo, dear <Ranger>, - a nice, slightly burring man with moustache said. - We've been waiting for you for a wong time! We are told about the tragic incident happened to your team and want to express our condolences to the <FromPlanet> pwanet. Fortunately, your team managed to gain a fair number of points. The team from <ToPlanet> took part in the final game not long ago. Now you need to gain 2 more points to win the championship. You will be able to do it if you are a success after the game tomorrow. And now you can go to the hotel and have a good rest before the match, - the bearded man said and sat back to his seat.

When you came to the middle-class hotel and filled all the necessary blanks, it was evening already. What will you do next?
loc.10.0:
In the morning, after a light breakfast, you went to the sports centre.

- Hewo, <Ranger>, - the bearded man who turned out to be the president of the jury was happy to see you. - We have been waiting for you already! Wet's go to the battlefield!

They took you to a spacious hall; there was a table with a fancy board and a chair in it. Journalists and automatic cameras were crowded behind the glass barrier. The board seemed very simple for the final game - just <clr>7 squares set in line <clrEnd>! Hardly anything difficult can be expected here. At least, you expected something trickier. Though only <clr>15<clrEnd> moves can be made during the whole game. 

- The <FromPlanet>'s team final game which will defined the world champion, is beginning! - the sports commentator announced.

So, it's time for the first move! Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.1:
- Tense moment... The player is deciding which checker it is going to be, - the sports commentator barged in.

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.2:
- A very unexpected move! - the caster said. - What do you have in mind, <Ranger>?

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.3:
- An expected move, - the caster explained authoritatively. - I would make it myself here!

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.4:
Judging from the spectators' reaction, your move was one of those unexpected. The caster didn't comment on it though.

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.5:
- A similar situation occurred during the final game for the champion title about, {[5..20]} years ago, - the caster was getting carried away in his own memories. - But then the board consisted of 113 squares... or 117? Heh, I have already forgotten...

You didn't listen to his further babbling and tried to concentrate on the game.

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.6:
An excellent move! - the caster said. - At least, it seems to me, it doesn't spoil the situation. And even if it does, then not too much...

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.7:
- A strange move, very strange... - the caster murmured. - I refuse to understand what our dear <Ranger> wants to achieve making it...

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.8:
- Do you know what does the current situation remind me of? - the caster exclaimed. - I visited the exhibition "Idiotic inventions" last year, and there was a showpiece there, "Traffic light for daltonians". Well, the current position is right to a tag!!!

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.10.9:
- We will know the name of the new champion within several moves, can you imagine that?- and the caster fell silent stunned by the depth of his own revelation.

Moves left: [p9]. Which checker is it going to be?
loc.27.0:
- No more moves! - the caster reported. The jury appeared from the door in the wall and hunched over the table. In a couple of minutes the president of the jury announced the verdict:

 - Ranger <Ranger> wost the final game and the <FromPlanet>' team remains on the second pwace. The team from the <ToPlanet> pwanet is the new champion!

Dejected, you returned to your spaceship. You failed the mission and they'll have no respect for you on the <FromPlanet> planet.
loc.28.0:
- No more moves! - the caster reported. The jury appeared from the door in the wall and hunched over the table. In a couple of minutes the president of the jury announced the verdict:

 - Ranger <Ranger> and his team from the <FromPlanet> pwanet are the winners of this tournament!!!

After the official ceremony they presented a bunch of flowers and an expensive cup to you. And the award in the amount of <Money> cr is waiting for you on <FromPlanet>! With such a pleasant thought in your head, you returned to the spaceport.
jump.5.desc:
You came to the library and at once saw an interesting book, <clr>"Rules of Hyper-jumping Plasma-checkers. Brief edition "<clrEnd>. Naturally, you started reading it right away! The text about the final game read:

"The rules for the HJPC final game are the following: the board has an unequal number of squares where <clr>one square is empty<clrEnd>, and the rest of them are filled with an equal number of black and white checkers. A checker can jump to an empty square, <clr>if the latter is neighbouring or situated in a checker <clrEnd> from it. Your task is <clr>to reverse the order of the white and black checkers in a specified amount of moves <clrEnd>. The number of points received for the winning, is calculated depending on the board's shape and size, as well as on the number of moves according to the following formulae..."

The text was followed by some formulae, quite boring for you, so you got back to your room and went to sleep.
